segmentation.text: to a vehicle which has entered the intersection
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion, not membership.

Same mapping as 'approaching the intersection' in the index: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c1 whose entrance end is X — st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end — the carrier is an approach to that intersection'; st.travel_region is c1's kind, st.intersection X's. Never read from distance or velocity.

Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed — kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above the halt tolerance — while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'). Contact is not a near miss; the near miss is the standard's bound.

'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate; 'which has entered the intersection' is its footprint overlapping X (rel.occupies), continuously since the observation at which it came from its approach carrier (f).

'From a different highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is v's approach carrier c2 (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c2 X) lying on a highway h2 (st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') on which the subject's carrier c1 does not lie. st.on_way is not nearness to a way: the relation is the map's.

Same mapping as 'or at a traffic-controlled intersection' in the index. DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'; the intersection is controlled where a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering it (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'; st.lane_enters ties the carrier to X).

'Vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions': per rel.oncoming's 'Not a stand-in for: the direction a road user approaches from — that is read through the carrier it approaches through ... and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction)'. The subject's carrier c1 and the carrier c2 v entered X from (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) have designated directions opposed within p.oncoming_heading_cos. 'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate.

'Is making a left turn' is the turn under way in X: the vehicle's heading change since its entry into X (rel.occupies), integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left') by the formula language's heading-since term, lying to the left between p.turn_heading_min and p.u_turn_heading_min. kin.yaw_rate is not a stand-in for road curvature: it is the vehicle's own turning.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a carrier c1 that enters an intersection X (st.lane_enters c1 X): the subject approaching X; except where X is controlled — a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X (dev.governs) — and except where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 (binder subject ↦ subject) applies to the subject.
obligation: Re-binding c1 and X as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps X and has overlapped it continuously since an observation at which v occupied a carrier c2 that enters X (st.lane_enters c2 X) and lies on a highway h2 (st.on_way c2 h2) on which c1 does not lie — excepting the pair where the designated directions of c1 and c2 (st.lane_direction) have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos and either the subject or v declares int.left_turn at X at this observation, or v's heading change since its latest entry into X (heading-since over kin.yaw_rate, step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is a turn to the left of at least p.turn_heading_min and below p.u_turn_heading_min: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'official' is a legal status; the device present and governing is its evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No device governs X or its carriers. Vehicle v entered X from carrier c2 on highway h2, on which the subject's carrier c1 does not lie, and is crossing X. The subject on c1 keeps kin.speed well above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject comes to rest on c1 short of X until v has cleared, then proceeds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs c1: the intersection is controlled.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X; v crossing X from a different highway on a conflicting path; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches the uncontrolled X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v is approaching X on its own carrier and has not entered X; the subject's closest approach to v is in conflict, but v is not a vehicle which has entered the intersection.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: At a skewed junction v entered X from c2 on another highway whose designated direction is opposed to c1's within p.oncoming_heading_cos, and v declares int.left_turn at X; the subject proceeds in conflict with v: the pair is excepted.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: skew tolerance of opposing intersection approaches

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading changes of a few degrees versus junction turns of about ninety degrees

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: midpoint between a right-angle turn and a full reversal of direction
